🇪🇺🇨🇳EU-China tensions are escalating.

Beijing has ordered Chinese companies and individuals not to cooperate with parts of an EU investigation into https://t.co/ev9bdAelsK’s proposed €2.2 billion takeover of German electronics retailer Ceconomy.

Brussels is investigating whether https://t.co/ev9bdAelsK benefited from Chinese state support that could distort competition.

The result is an unusual regulatory confrontation: Chinese authorities are telling companies not to provide information that European regulators are demanding.

If https://t.co/ev9bdAelsK cannot satisfy Brussels, the EU could impose conditions—or potentially block the acquisition.
featured_items.translation_zh:
🇪🇺🇨🇳欧盟与中国的紧张关系正在升级。

北京已命令中国企业和个人不要配合欧盟一项调查的部分内容，该调查涉及 JD.com 拟以 22 亿欧元收购德国电子产品零售商 Ceconomy。

布鲁塞尔正在调查 JD.com 是否受益于可能扭曲竞争的中国国家支持。

其结果是一场不同寻常的监管对峙：中国当局正在要求企业不要提供欧洲监管机构所要求的信息。

如果 JD.com 无法让布鲁塞尔满意，欧盟可能会施加条件——或者可能阻止这笔收购。

A statement from China’s Ministry of Justice on Wednesday condemned the probe as “undue extraterritorial jurisdiction measures”, ordering that “no organisation or individual may execute or assist in the execution”.

In May, the European Commission opened an in-depth investigation to assess whether JD.com proposed takeover of German retailer Ceconomy would “distort the EU internal market” because of the Chinese company’s alleged receipt of state subsidies.

It marked the latest in a succession of inquiries opened under the FSR, a competition sector tool that requires companies under investigation to hand over reams of information within short deadlines.

This is the second time Beijing has used a blocking order to ensure entities do not comply with such a probe, having issued a similar decree with regard to a case centred on airport scanner maker Nuctech in May. Nuctech unsuccessfully sued the commission in 2024, alleging that dawn raids on its Dutch and Polish premises caused reputational harm and that it was being asked to disclose information that would force it to violate Chinese criminal laws.

Last month, meanwhile, wind turbine manufacturer Goldwind asked for its own FSR case to be suspended because the commission’s request for information went beyond the scope of the investigation. The EU’s General Court ruled against Goldwind’s claim, saying it was too speculative.

The Chinese justice ministry statement, issued jointly with the Ministry of Commerce, accused the EU of “arbitrarily demanding extensive and unnecessary information about China from the Chinese entity”.

The proposed US$2.5 billion transaction would see JD.com acquire Europe’s largest electronics retailer, Ceconomy. The German firm specialises in consumer electronics and home appliances.

Geopolitechs, a Substack newsletter that analyses Chinese policy decisions, noted that while Beijing had not ordered the EU to terminate its investigation, the directive still put JD.com in an awkward position.

“What China is objecting to is the commission extending its investigative powers into Chinese territory by requiring Chinese companies, banks and other institutions to cooperate and provide information that Beijing considers excessively broad in scope,” the newsletter read.

“Providing information to the commission could violate the Chinese prohibition, while refusing to provide it could lead the commission to conclude that JD.com has failed to cooperate and draw adverse inferences.”

北京已禁止中国实体协助欧洲联盟依据该集团的《外国补贴条例》（FSR）对电商巨头 JD.com（京东）展开的调查。

中国司法部周三发布声明，谴责这项调查是“不当域外管辖措施”，并下令“任何组织和个人不得执行或者协助执行”。

今年 5 月，欧洲委员会启动深入调查，以评估 JD.com 拟收购德国零售商 Ceconomy 的交易，是否会因这家中国公司被指获得国家补贴而“扭曲欧盟内部市场”。

这是根据 FSR 启动的一系列调查中的最新一起。FSR 是一项竞争领域工具，要求被调查公司在很短期限内提交大量信息。

这是北京第二次使用阻断令，以确保相关实体不配合此类调查。此前，北京曾在 5 月就一起围绕机场扫描仪制造商 Nuctech（同方威视）的案件发布类似命令。Nuctech 曾在 2024 年起诉欧盟委员会但未获成功，称其在荷兰和波兰场所遭到突击检查造成声誉损害，并称其被要求披露的信息会迫使其违反中国刑法。

与此同时，上个月，风力涡轮机制造商 Goldwind（金风科技）要求暂停其自身的 FSR 案件，理由是欧盟委员会的信息索取超出了调查范围。欧盟普通法院驳回了 Goldwind 的主张，称其过于推测性。

中国司法部与商务部联合发布的声明指责欧盟“任意要求中国实体提供大量且不必要的涉华信息”。

这项拟议的 25 亿美元交易将使 JD.com 收购欧洲最大的电子产品零售商 Ceconomy。这家德国公司专注于消费电子产品和家用电器。

分析中国政策决定的 Substack 通讯 Geopolitechs 指出，尽管北京没有命令欧盟终止调查，但该指令仍使 JD.com 处于尴尬境地。

该通讯写道：“中国反对的是，欧盟委员会通过要求中国公司、银行和其他机构配合并提供北京认为范围过于宽泛的信息，将其调查权力延伸到中国领土内。”

“向欧盟委员会提供信息可能违反中国的禁令，而拒绝提供信息则可能导致欧盟委员会认定 JD.com 未能合作，并作出不利推断。”
